experiment: HLS-S3b changes x exogenous observation-opportunity factorial

design.modality: B2 full one-to-one matching (same feasible action set in all cells)
design.schedule: deterministic recurrent alternation base/transient; transitions at multiples of interval
design.observation_rule: for every pair-period, an exogenous shared uniform determines feedback availability; policy does not see masks before action; selected reward is observed iff its pair-period mask is available
design.reward: Bernoulli(c_ik(t)); realized reward contributes whether or not feedback is observed
design.opportunity_stream: random.Random(seed XOR 0x0B5E7A), period-agent-task; nested p=.25/.75 thresholds
design.calibration: first 9 periods use the predeclared E1 three-matching cycle; counts in performance and are subject to same observation mask

algorithms.SW-UCB: same estimator; period-global W=1214, xi=2.0; empirical window mean + sqrt(xi log(max(2,min(t+1,W))/n))

design.oracles: exact maximum true-mean complete matching by six-permutation enumeration; independent of feedback availability
design.rho_definition: rho_opportunity = p_observe * stability_interval; not a performance law; effective observations are separately measured from executed-and-observed pairs
design.lambda_rho_interpretation: p_observe is the exogenous per-pair opportunity rate; lambda_effective_ik is estimated from observations actually obtained after execution, and rho_effective is its mean count per stability interval
design.hypothesis_status: factorial levels fixed before execution; no directional rejection criterion frozen pre-campaign; directional assessment exploratory
design.exploratory_directional_hypothesis: frequent changes with high opportunity availability may improve SW-UCB relative to UCB1 more than frequent changes with low availability; assessed by difference-in-differences of paired regret SW-UCB minus UCB1
